subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what token containment, scope, and privacy rules should it use?
rationale: This is a valid Slack feature gap, but it would handle event-scoped tokens and workspace-wide search results, so automation should not choose the security boundary or product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, redaction, docs, focused tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search first
options.body: Design one Slack search contract that deliberately covers both RTS and any user-token legacy search behavior before implementation.

options.title: Defer workspace search
options.body: Keep Slack workspace search out of OpenClaw until maintainers are ready to own the token, scope, and live-validation burden.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, redaction, docs, focused tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest merged history on Slack assistant lifecycle and the broadest related Slack action-surface PR history.
